org: U.S. Web Design System (USWDS) — GSA / Technology Transformation Services
accessNotes: The guidance page is static and was read fully (web_fetch markdown plus raw HTML). The two example charts are inline Adobe Illustrator SVGs; their CSS (colours, stroke widths, dash patterns, font sizes) was read from the SVG source, and the rendered figure cards were screenshotted in a headless browser. USWDS data-viz guidance is 'guidance-only' with no component code and no dedicated chart palette, so colours below are those used in the official examples (they are standard USWDS system colours).
summary: Government product/content design system whose data-visualisation guidance is accessibility-first rather than stylistic: plain-language heading and summary above the chart, a single colour for same-category bars, dash patterns and point markers to separate lines without colour, an sr-only data table, and a linked 'Source:' line. Example charts are simple, flat and sit in a white bordered, rounded card using USWDS primary blue #005EA2 and warm orange.

colors.categoricalNotes: No official chart palette. Examples use primary blue #005EA2 and orange #FA9441 (orange line) with darker orange #C05600 markers. Guidance: 'Simplify color selection and don't reuse colors for different variables or within a particular variable'; for multi-variant bars 'use discrete, high contrast colors or textured fill'; same-category bars in one colour.
colors.notes: From example SVG CSS: axis lines stroke #71767A at 1px (non-scaling); gridlines #DFE1E2 1px; label text fill #1B1B1B; line series #005EA2 (5-6px, round caps) and #FA9441 (5px, dashed 4 1) with markers #005EA2 / #C05600 r=8 in a ~1020px viewBox. Card summary text uses USWDS 'text-base' grey. Must meet contrast requirements.

typography.fallback: -apple-system, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

axisTitle.placement: omitted; measure named in legend ('Visits (in millions)') or summary

source.style: regular, 'Source:' followed by a hyperlink to the original data

typography.notes: Chart heading is an HTML h4 inside the card, not part of the SVG. Example SVG text sizes in viewBox units: axis labels 24-27, legend/category labels 25-26 (rendered roughly 12-14px). Bar example SVG declares MyriadPro-Regular (Illustrator export) but renders in the page sans-serif.

structure.gridlines: Light grey (#DFE1E2) 1px lines along the value axis only: horizontal in the line chart, vertical in the horizontal bar chart.
structure.axisLine: Both axes drawn: thin 1px grey (#71767A) L-shaped axes (left + bottom).
structure.zeroLine: 'Line charts origin should start at zero, unless clearly noted.'
structure.unitPlacement: In the legend label ('Visits (in millions)') and in the summary text.
structure.frame: Card container: 1px border, white background, rounded corners (radius-md), padding-2, max-width tablet; heading, summary, chart and source line all inside the card.
structure.background: white card on the page background

legend.placement: top, above the plot (line chart: spread across the full width; bar chart: left-aligned with plot area)
legend.title: none
legend.swatchShape: line sample with marker (matching dash pattern) for lines; filled rectangle for bars
legend.notes: A legend is shown even for a single bar series to name the measure.

marks.bars: Horizontal bars, single colour #005EA2, square corners, bar thickness roughly 2.5x the gap, sorted descending, category labels right-aligned (wrapping to two lines).
marks.lines: Thick lines (5-6px) with round caps and circular markers (r≈8) at each point; the second series is dashed (4 1) and uses a darker marker colour than its line to distinguish without colour.
marks.points: Circle markers; triangles, squares or other simple shapes are acceptable.
marks.notes: Stacked bars for multi-variant data only if communicating the sum matters; use textures/high-contrast colours.

labels.dates: Abbreviated month with period and day ('Mar. 1').
labels.notes: Provide textual representation of axis values and labels (not embedded in an image).

furniture.title: Clear plain-language heading stating the point ('The five most-visited national parks of 2019'), followed by a summary paragraph that states the intended message and explains the measure.
furniture.source: Below the chart: 'Source: ' + link to the original data (e.g. 'Source: National Park Service'); the sr-only table is aria-describedby the source line.
furniture.other: Visually hidden (usa-sr-only) data table with caption; SVG hidden with aria-hidden="true".

annotations: Narrative goes in text: 'Clearly state the author's intended message as text'; provide trends or statistical summaries in plain text for screen readers.
layout: Card max-width 'tablet'; chart SVG scales to card width.
interaction: 'Reduce interaction' - the message must not depend on hover or mouse use; choose charting tools with keyboard and screen-reader support.
accessibility: Core of the guidance: equivalent access via sr-only data table (usa-sr-only) and aria-hidden SVG; plain-text summary; meet colour contrast; dash patterns, point styles and textures so colour isn't required; manual accessibility testing (Section 508).

discouraged: unfamiliar chart types for audiences of unknown data literacy
charts with more than two or three concepts
chartTypes.notes: Prefer common visualization types; 'Don't try to do too much.'

distinctiveRules.rule: Each chart lives in a white bordered card with rounded corners containing heading, summary paragraph, chart and source line.
distinctiveRules.quote:
…

distinctiveRules.rule: A plain-language summary paragraph in grey sits between the heading and the chart and states the conclusion.
distinctiveRules.quote: Clearly state the author's intended message as text.

distinctiveRules.rule: Source line below the chart: 'Source: ' followed by a hyperlink to the original data.
distinctiveRules.quote: Original data linked. We linked back to the original source data

distinctiveRules.rule: Multiple lines distinguished without colour: one solid, one dashed (4 1) with contrasting marker colour; circle markers at every data point.
distinctiveRules.quote: One is a solid color, and the other uses both a dash pattern and a color contrast between the line and the indicators.

distinctiveRules.rule: Bars measuring the same variable share a single colour (#005EA2).
distinctiveRules.quote: The bars are the same color because the data is categorically the same

distinctiveRules.rule: Thin grey (#71767A) left and bottom axis lines, light grey (#DFE1E2) gridlines along the value axis only, no ticks.
Legend above the plot (no title), even for a single series, used to name the measure and unit.
Value axis starts at zero unless clearly noted.
distinctiveRules.quote: Line charts origin should start at zero, unless clearly noted.

distinctiveRules.rule: Every chart ships a visually hidden data table and hides the SVG from assistive tech.
distinctiveRules.quote: Provide an screen-reader accessible data table ... using the class usa-sr-only ... hide the visualization using the attribute aria-hidden="true"

distinctiveRules.rule: Don't require hover/interaction to understand the message.
distinctiveRules.quote: Your audience shouldn't be required to interact with a visualization to understand its message.

referenceImages.describes: White card with thin dark border and rounded corners. Bold sans heading 'The five most-visited national parks of 2019' top-left, grey multi-line summary paragraph beneath. Legend above plot, left-aligned to plot area: blue square + 'Visits (in millions)'. Horizontal bars all #005EA2, sorted descending, square ends, thick bars with modest gaps; category labels right-aligned in two lines ('Grand Canyon / National Park'). Thin grey left axis and bottom axis, light grey vertical gridlines at 0-14 step 2, numeric labels below, no ticks. 'Source: National Park Service' (link, underlined, with external-link icon) at bottom-left of the card.

Line chart in the same card style: grey summary text above; legend at top with line samples (orange dashed with brown-orange dot 'Franklin D. Roosevelt' on the left, solid blue with blue dot 'Theodore Roosevelt' on the right). Orange #FA9441 dashed line with #C05600 circle markers; blue #005EA2 solid line with blue markers; markers at every day. Light grey horizontal gridlines at 25/50/75/100, grey left and bottom axis lines, y labels 0-100 left, x labels 'Mar. 1'...'Mar. 7'. 'Source: Google Trends' link below.
